riddle: I begin with T, I end with T, and I have T inside me. What am I?
hint: You pour from me into cups.

riddle: I begin with E, I end with E, and I usually hold just one letter. What am I?
I'm a word of only three syllables, yet I contain all twenty-six letters. What am I?
hint: You learnt me as a song in nursery.

riddle: Which letter of the alphabet can you drink hot with milk, sugar and a bit of ginger?
Which letter of the alphabet is full of salt water, waves and ships?
Which letter of the alphabet buzzes around flowers and makes honey?
Which letter of the alphabet is always asking for a reason?
Which letter of the alphabet do you use to see with?
I go up with every single birthday and never come back down. What am I?
hint: Candles on the cake keep count.

riddle: Say my name out loud and you break me. What am I?
You whisper me and beg people not to tell. Once I'm shared with everyone, I no longer exist. What am I?
I shout back at you across mountains and empty halls, but I only ever repeat your own words. What am I?
I follow you all day in the sunshine and copy every move you make, but I vanish in total darkness. What am I?
hint: Look at the ground on a sunny day.

riddle: I fly without wings, I heal old wounds, and once I'm spent you can never buy me back. What am I?
I'm always exactly one day away. The moment you reach me, I change my name to today. What am I?
hint: Never put off till me what you can do now.

riddle: Just one day ago I was called today, and you will never see me again. What am I?
I'm lighter than a feather, yet even the strongest wrestler can't hold me for more than a few minutes. What am I?
I belong to you, yet your friends use me far more often than you do. What am I?
The more of me there is, the less you can see, and a single candle is enough to push me back. What am I?
The more you dig out of me, the bigger I get. What am I?
The more of me you take, the more of me you leave behind. What am I?
Which letter sits right in the middle of both March and April?
hint: Count the letters in each month.

riddle: I begin with IS, I end with AND, LA sits in my middle, and water surrounds me on every side. What am I?
I have a bed but never sleep, and a mouth but never speak, and I keep running all the way to the sea. What am I?
I have a face and two hands but no arms, and I hang on your wall ticking all day. What am I?
I have a spine but no bones, and people warn you never to judge me by my cover. What am I?
Which room has no doors, no walls and no windows, but tastes great on a pizza?
hint: It grows in damp, shady spots.

riddle: Which tree fits in your hand, because every hand already has one?
Which bow can never be tied, but shows off seven colours after the rain?
hint: Look up when the sun comes out after a shower.

riddle: Which key can't open a single lock, but swings from trees and steals bananas?
Forwards I twinkle in the night sky; spell me backwards and I'm rodents in the gutter. What am I forwards?
I'm one word for a creature that hangs upside down at night and for the thing a batsman swings. What am I?
I'm one word for the rough outer skin of a tree and for the sound a dog makes. What am I?
I'm one word for the season when leaves drop and for tripping down to the ground. What am I?
hint: Americans use me instead of autumn.

riddle: I'm one word for the land along the edge of a river and for the place that keeps your money. What am I?
I'm one word for a sticky brown fruit and for a romantic evening out with someone. What am I?
hint: Also a day on the calendar.

riddle: I'm one word for what your phone does when someone calls and for the band you slip onto a finger. What am I?
I'm one word for a small squeaky animal that nibbles cheese and for the thing you click beside your laptop. What am I?
Which number sounds exactly like the word meaning 'as well'?
Which number sounds exactly like the past tense of 'eat'?
I can be cracked, told, made up, and played on someone. What am I?
I fill a whole room the moment you flick a switch, yet I take up no space at all. What am I?
What do you call a bear that has lost all of its teeth?
hint: A chewy sweet shares the name.

riddle: What do you call cheese that belongs to somebody else?
Which key on a keyboard is an astronaut's favourite?
What do you call a strawberry that is feeling sad?
Which room of the house do ghosts always stay out of?
What kind of music are balloons most scared of?
hint: What happens when you poke one with a pin?

riddle: I'm silent and catching. I show up when you're sleepy or bored, and just reading about me might make you do me. What am I?
I'm a secret word you type to get in; forget me and you're locked out of your own account. What am I?
hint: Don't write me on a sticky note.

riddle: I hold nearly every word you know, lined up from A to Z, and I tell you what each one means. What am I?
I visit you most nights, show you things that aren't real, and slip away soon after you wake. What am I?
hint: You have me in your sleep.

riddle: Which pet animal is hiding inside the word 'education'?
Which number is hiding inside the word 'often'?
Put the thing that rises every morning in front of something that blooms, and you get a tall yellow plant. What is it?
hint: Its seeds are a crunchy snack.

riddle: Join something that burns with what you do at the office, and you get the loud, colourful show that fills the sky on Diwali. What is it?
Look it up in any dictionary and this word is always spelled wrong. Which word is it?
I'm a five-letter word, but add two letters to me and I become shorter. What am I?
My name has three double letters in a row, and my job is keeping a company's accounts in order. What am I?
Which letter of the alphabet is also a female sheep?
Which two letters, said aloud, describe the feeling of being jealous?
I'm a building that starts with P, ends with E, and handles thousands of letters every day. What am I?
I'm a four-letter time of day. Written in capitals, I read the same forwards, backwards and upside down. What am I?
Forwards I'm a huge weight; spell me backwards and I'm a word for refusing. What am I forwards?
I'm an odd number, but take away my first letter and I become even. What am I?
I'm a three-letter word meaning 'not many'. Add two letters and there are even less of me. What am I?
I'm fixed to the wall by your gate and I'm only seven letters long, yet I'm often stuffed with dozens of letters. What am I?
I can be broken without being dropped and kept without being held. I'm given, never bought. What am I?
hint: You make me and hope to keep me.

riddle: I show up once in a minute, twice in a moment, and never in a thousand years. What am I?
hint: Look at the spelling, not the clock.

riddle: Which letter is found right in the middle of nowhere?
Which letter sits at the centre of gravity?
I'm a five-letter word you stand in at the bank. Remove my last four letters and I'm still pronounced exactly the same. What am I?
hint: I sound like a single letter.

riddle: Spell me backwards and I become sweet treats after dinner; forwards I'm how you feel the night before exams. What am I forwards?
Forwards I'm where you keep your socks; spell me backwards and I'm what you get for good work. What am I forwards?
I'm one word for a student in a classroom and for the black dot at the centre of your eye. What am I?
I'm the underside of your foot or shoe, I'm also a flat fish, and I sound just like your spirit. What am I?
I beat inside your chest. Shuffle my letters and I become the planet you live on. What am I?
Said one way I roll down your cheek; said another way I'm what you do to a sheet of paper. What am I?
I'm hot, sandy and dry. Add one more S and I become the sweet you eat after dinner. What am I?
I'm a grain ground into atta for rotis. Drop my first letter and I become the warmth of a summer afternoon. What am I?
I'm what your ears do in class. Shuffle my letters and you get what you must be to do me well. What am I?
Which is the longest word in English, since there's a whole mile between its first and last letters?
hint: You do it when you're happy.

riddle: Only two common English words end in G-R-Y. One is 'hungry'. What is the other?
hint: How you feel when someone cuts the queue.

riddle: What do you call a fish that has no eyes?
What do you call a deer that has no eyes?
What do you call a boomerang that never comes back?
Which smooth-skinned cousin of the peach is a vampire's favourite fruit?
Which cup can't hold a single drop of water, yet won't go away until someone gives you a fright?
Which part of a fish could you also use to weigh your vegetables?
Which mountain is the laziest of them all?
hint: It would ___ rest if it could.

riddle: What do you call a snowman in the middle of summer?
hint: Give it a few hours of sun.

riddle: I tick all night and go off every morning, yet I never leave the little table beside your bed. What am I?
What do you call a kangaroo that spends all day lying on the sofa?
What do you call a bee that just can't make up its mind?
What do you call a dinosaur that knows lots of words that mean the same thing?
hint: Its name ends the way lots of dinosaur names do.

riddle: What do you call an elephant that doesn't matter at all?
hint: Think of a big grey animal with a trunk.

riddle: I'm catching, yet no doctor treats me. I can make your sides ache and your eyes water without hurting you. What am I?
I pass from ear to ear, grow a little bigger each time I'm retold, and nobody can say who started me. What am I?
Rich people need it, poor people have it, and if you eat only it you'll starve. What is it?
Which part of your face is hiding inside the word 'machine'?
I'm a past-tense verb and the only common English word that ends in the letters M-T. What am I?
Which two letters, said aloud, mean 'far more than is needed'?
hint: Say letters from the end of the alphabet.

riddle: Take the whole away from me, and some is still left. What word am I?
hint: A compound word; healthy food is often called this.

riddle: I can go up a chimney when I'm down, but I can't go down a chimney when I'm up. What am I?
Say me one way and I'm sixty seconds; say me another way and I'm incredibly tiny. What am I?
Spell out every number from one to ninety-nine in English. Which vowel never shows up even once?
Which whole number, spelled out in English, has all its letters in alphabetical order?
Which number, written out in English, has exactly as many letters as the number itself?
Shuffle my nine letters and they spell 'dirty room', which is often how students leave me. What am I?
Rearrange my ten letters and you get 'moon starer', which is exactly what I do for a living. What am I?
Rearrange the letters of 'they see' and you get the very things that do the seeing. What are they?
What do you call a factory that only makes products that are just okay?
Which kind of 'tea' is the hardest to swallow, because it's the opposite of fantasy?
hint: Listen for the 'ty' sound at the end.

riddle: What do you call an alligator wearing a vest?
What do you call a long line of people waiting to get a haircut?
What do you call a belt made entirely of wristwatches?
What do you call a bear caught out in light rain?
hint: A big brown bear with a similar name.

riddle: What do you call a javelin thrower who's feeling nervous?
Which vegetable does a ship's captain fear the most?
hint: It sounds like water getting in.

riddle: I'm a nine-letter word meaning 'surprising'. Remove one letter at a time and a real word is left at every step, down to a single letter. What am I?
I'm a pleasant smell. Remove my first letter, or my second instead, and I still sound exactly the same. What am I?
I'm a verb that means both wiping fine powder off a shelf and sprinkling fine powder onto a cake. What am I?
hint: A word that is its own opposite.

riddle: I mean both 'went away' and 'stayed behind', and I'm also a direction you can turn. What am I?
With a capital letter I describe people from Warsaw; with a small letter I'm what makes old shoes shine. What am I?
Written in capitals, this five-letter word still reads the same when you turn the page upside down. Fill the gap: 'She ___ ten laps in the pool every morning.' What is the word?
